dialect.guess: MetaWare Technologies COBOL (translated/ported, likely targeting GnuCOBOL or similar open-source runtime)
evidence: ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL (translated from mainframe sequential)
DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA (European locale, typical of French mainframe COBOL)
LABEL RECORD STANDARD / BLOCK CONTAINS 0 RECORDS (mainframe-style FD clauses)

purpose.summary: This program processes stock movement files resulting from the merger of two subsidiary companies ('filiales'). It reads two input movement files (FHV030 and FHV031), filters/excludes certain records based on matching criteria, and writes the retained movements to an output file (FGS40). It also reads a company code file (FNSOC) and a parameter file (FPARAM).

notable_features: COMP-3 packed decimal fields (monetary and quantity fields)
MetaWare COBOL translator comments marking transformed SELECT statements (Tr-Select-Sequential)
Original mainframe SELECT statements preserved as comments alongside translated LINE SEQUENTIAL versions
French-language comments and field names throughout
Sequence numbers in columns 73-80 indicating mainframe origin
Multiple input files with complex record layouts (146-byte and 179-byte records)
88-level condition names for file status flags (DEBUT/FIN)
verdict.notes: The file was originally written for an IBM mainframe environment (evidenced by fixed-format, sequence numbers, LABEL RECORD STANDARD, BLOCK CONTAINS 0, COMP-3, and French mainframe conventions) and was subsequently translated by 'MetaWare Technologies Cobol-Translater 0.9.16' in 2016 to run on a non-mainframe platform using LINE SEQUENTIAL file organization. The source is truncated at 16000 chars (about half the full 32400-byte file), so the PROCEDURE DIVISION is not visible, but all structural indicators confirm genuine production COBOL.
